source_name: eKariera.sk - employer profile directory
why_relevant: Company-indexed job directory; the /firmy/<slug> structure gives a quick way to enumerate SK employers in the banking sector and to spot smaller banks, leasing arms and processors that a keyword search misses.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Pilsen Global Center - open positions (CZ, SK-adjacent)
why_relevant: Diebold Nixdorf runs no visible SK hiring hub; its regional ATM/self-service software and support capacity for CEE - including Slovak deployments and Vynamic-branded software - is staffed out of the Pilsen global center. Watching Pilsen roles is the practical proxy for DN's delivery capacity aimed at Slovak banks.

source_name: Pracuj.sk
why_relevant: Newer-generation SK job portal (Pracuj group) gaining share; worth registering now because employer migration between portals is common and losing a channel silently creates blind spots in longitudinal hiring series.

source_name: Recruiteri.sk - directory of Slovak job servers and recruiters
why_relevant: Maintained local-language index of Slovak job servers and recruitment agencies. Best single starting point for periodically re-checking whether the portal landscape has shifted, and for enumerating specialist IT/finance recruitment agencies whose own listings often carry the most explicit platform requirements.

source_name: Euronet Slovakia (euronet.sk) – independent ATM deployer corporate site
why_relevant: Euronet is the largest non-bank (IAD) ATM deployer in SK; its own site carries network positioning, fee/DCC terms, ATM locator and outsourcing offers to banks/retailers — the primary window into the non-bank ATM buying layer.

source_name: Euronet ATM Solutions (euronetatms.com) – outsourcing/ATM-as-a-service product site
why_relevant: Group-level product/solution pages (ATM outsourcing, CIT ATMs, branch automation) show what Euronet sells to banks and retailers across CEE, i.e. the competitive offer set facing hardware/managed-service vendors in SK.

source_name: Loomis SK – cash-in-transit and ATM management (sk.loomis.com / loomis.sk)
why_relevant: Loomis SK runs CIT, cash processing under NBS licence and ATM replenishment/first-line ATM management for SK banks; its product and branch pages map the cash-cycle service layer and identify who actually touches ATM/recycler estates.

source_name: G4S / Securitas Slovakia – security and cash services presence pages
why_relevant: G4S Security Services (SK) is described as the largest private security provider in SK and includes money transport; establishes the second CIT pole alongside Loomis and the Securitas-group ownership overlay.

source_name: Brink's Czech/CEE cash solutions site (brinks.cz) – regional CIT reference
why_relevant: No distinct SK Brink's site surfaced; the CZ entity documents the CEE CIT lineage (Group 4 Securitas → G4S Cash Services → Brink's) and partnerships that shape the neighbouring/cross-border cash-handling market relevant to SK.

source_name: COOP Jednota Slovensko – COOP miniBANKOMAT / CashBack service pages
why_relevant: COOP Jednota runs the largest retail cash-at-checkout network in SK (~2,000 stores, limit raised to EUR 100, partner banks UniCredit, ČSOB, SLSP, 365.bank) — the clearest evidence of retail as a cash-access channel competing with ATMs, plus named bank/scheme partnerships.

source_name: Lidl Slovenská republika – corporate press room (spolocnost.lidl.sk)
why_relevant: Lidl SK announces checkout technology rollouts (self-checkout, e-labels) in its own press releases — a primary record of self-service checkout deployment volumes and timing at the largest discounter.

source_name: Forbes.sk – retail technology / self-checkout coverage
why_relevant: Business media aggregate self-checkout counts across chains (Lidl, Kaufland, Tesco ~half of transactions, Billa 52 stores) that retailers do not publish uniformly — the best cross-chain deployment benchmark found.

source_name: Dopravný podnik Bratislava (DPB) – news and fare-system announcements
why_relevant: DPB is the buyer of Bratislava's open-loop contactless ticketing ('Kartuj', succeeded by 'Tapni sa'); its news section documents launch dates, accepted schemes and on-board validator changes — a direct transit-payments buyer record.

source_name: imhd.sk – Bratislava/Košice public transport documentation wiki
why_relevant: Enthusiast-maintained but unusually detailed archive of fare technology in BA and KE — validator generations, card acceptance rules, ticket-machine card upgrades; often names equipment and dates that operators omit, and links onward to operator documents.

source_name: DPMK Košice – verejné obstarávanie and contract register
why_relevant: DPMK tenders on-board computers, APC and contactless validators (reported supply of ~1,100 validators by EMtest); its procurement pages and transparent-contract register name suppliers, values and delivery schedules directly.

source_name: Slovenská pošta – services and SKPAY payment institution pages
source_subtype: state operator service pages + PDF terms
why_relevant: Post counters are a major non-bank cash and payment channel (SIPO, cash-in/out, SKPAY as payment/e-money institution, joint venture with Poštová banka); the terms documents reveal the counter service and device model.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) – card issuing/acquiring statistics
why_relevant: Monthly card, ATM and POS transaction statistics give the denominator for the cash-cycle story (ATM withdrawals declining vs card payments) against which retail cashback and self-checkout deployments should be read.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska – payments and statistics sections
why_relevant: NBS licenses cash processors (Loomis processes under an NBS licence), publishes payment-instrument statistics and the reporting measures (e.g. opatrenie 11/2023) that define what ATM/POS data exists — sets the regulatory frame for the whole cash-handling layer.

source_name: Banky.sk – card/ATM count explainer series
why_relevant: Repackages NBS/SBA figures into dated, citable ATM and card counts; useful as a quick cross-check and for spotting when official series change, though always to be traced back to NBS/SBA.

source_name: Pravda / oPeniazoch (openiazoch.zoznam.sk) – cash-access and retail cashback reporting
why_relevant: Consumer/finance media enumerate which chains offer cash-at-checkout, limits and participating banks — the practical cross-retailer map of the cash-access layer that no single retailer publishes.

source_name: ifirmy.sk / FinStat-style SK company registers – CIT and deployer entity profiles
why_relevant: Company registers resolve the legal entities behind the cash-cycle layer (Loomis SK a.s., G4S SK entities, EuroNET Slovakia s.r.o.), giving IČO keys for cross-linking to ÚVO profiles, CRZ contracts and financial statements.

source_name: Profesia.sk job listings as a deployment/operations signal
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: CIT and deployer hiring ('pracovník dotácie bankomatov' = ATM replenishment staff, by region) signals estate size, expansion and which cities a cash operator actually serves — data not otherwise published.

source_name: Relife.sk and similar SK consumer explainers on Euronet ATM fees
why_relevant: Consumer-facing critiques of independent ATM fee/DCC practice are a proxy for IAD commercial model and public perception, and often list where Euronet ATMs are sited (airports, tourist zones, retail).

source_name: EMtest – transit validator/on-board systems supplier (SK)
why_relevant: Named in reporting as supplier of ~1,100 contactless-capable validators to DPMK Košice; a domestic incumbent in transit fare hardware and therefore a direct competitor/partner candidate in the non-bank payments buyer layer.

source_name: TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) — notice search, SK country filter
why_relevant: Mandatory EU-wide publication venue for above-threshold SK tenders; contract award notices name the winning vendor, value and CPV, making it the backbone for vendor/competitor mapping around SK banks, NBS, state financial institutions and payment infrastructure. Notices exist in both SK and EN.

source_name: TED Search API v3 (api.ted.europa.eu) + bulk XML packages
why_relevant: Machine-readable, no-auth access to all TED notices: expert query syntax, up to 15,000 docs paginated (250/page), a stream/token mode without that cap, plus daily and monthly bulk XML packages. This is the only scalable way to build a longitudinal SK banking/payments CPV vendor dataset.

source_name: Úrad pre verejné obstarávanie — Vestník verejného obstarávania (eForms)
why_relevant: SK national mirror/origin of the same eForms notices that flow to TED, published every business day with full-text and criteria search. Captures below-threshold contracts that never reach TED, and gives the SK-language wording of scope (bankomat, platobný terminál, kartové centrum) needed for the glossary.

source_name: Plán obnovy a odolnosti SR — official portal (planobnovy.sk)
why_relevant: Slovakia's RRF portal; the 'Efektívna verejná správa a digitalizácia' component documents digitalisation investments, milestones and the IT methodology governing how RRF-funded IT is bought. Supplies the funding-side context and named calls that later surface as TED/UVO tenders touching financial-sector IT.
